searchText: quick question: will `ShardState.data` be the root of the cross-linked object? I think `ShardState.data` is the "real" state root ie. not including the protocol-level auxiliary stuff ah okay, so it's only the state root, it wouldn't include directly a reference to a receipt tree. i.e. for that we should use `ShardState.latest_block_root` and then reference it through the shard block header? aaah, sorry, it would include a receipt root too another question i had was: let's say we want to prove a receipt from one shard to a second shard. is it okay to prove against the hash of an old beacon block? i.e can we expect people will store beacon blocks for some time, or we'll have to go through `BeaconState.state_roots` or `BeaconState.historical_roots` of a *very recent* block? https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase1/beacon-chain.md#shardstate <@!273808422753796097> in here you mean `data` is the real state root, while `latest_block_root` is some protocol wrapped version of the same? It is a bit confusing to me, because the `apply_shard_transition` only cares about `latest_block_root`. The phase2 spec draft PR has some initial take on the use of the shard data roots and updating of phase1 code to do execution. Should be useful to you <@259648573401071617> > It is a bit confusing to me, because the apply_shard_transition only cares about latest_block_root. This is because the beacon chain code itself does not verify the shard transitions That's up to the committees and the fraud proof mechanism

excerpts.author: s1na
excerpts.content: quick question: will `ShardState.data` be the root of the cross-linked object?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: I think `ShardState.data` is the "real" state root

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: ie. not including the protocol-level auxiliary stuff

excerpts.author: s1na
excerpts.content: ah okay, so it's only the state root, it wouldn't include directly a reference to a receipt tree. i.e. for that we should use `ShardState.latest_block_root` and then reference it through the shard block header?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: aaah, sorry, it would include a receipt root too

excerpts.author: s1na
excerpts.content: another question i had was: let's say we want to prove a receipt from one shard to a second shard. is it okay to prove against the hash of an old beacon block? i.e can we expect people will store beacon blocks for some time, or we'll have to go through `BeaconState.state_roots` or `BeaconState.historical_roots` of a *very recent* block?

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content:
https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase1/beacon-chain.md#shardstate

<@!273808422753796097> in here you mean `data` is the real state root, while `latest_block_root` is some protocol wrapped version of the same?

It is a bit confusing to me, because the `apply_shard_transition` only cares about `latest_block_root`.

excerpts.content: The phase2 spec draft PR has some initial take on the use of the shard data roots and updating of phase1 code to do execution. Should be useful to you <@259648573401071617>
